concepts.preferred_label: Pulmonary Atresia with Ventricular Septal Defect
concepts.why: The patient has pulmonary atresia with ventricular septal defect and a patent ductus arteriosus, as revealed by echocardiography.
The patient has a low platelet count, a prolonged platelet aggregation time, and a provisional diagnosis of immune thrombocytopenia was made.
The patient has a low oxygen saturation level, which is consistent with cyanosis.
The patient has a patent ductus arteriosus, as revealed by echocardiography.
The patient has a ventricular septal defect, as revealed by echocardiography.
The patient has a low oxygen saturation level and required prostaglandin infusion and a systemic-to-pulmonary shunt operation, which is consistent with respiratory distress.
